about_blocks.text: Sober Maintenance is a private addiction recovery coaching service run by one person, Trevor Smith, from Toronto. It is not a rehab centre. There are no beds, no group sessions and no clinic to walk into. Trevor meets clients in their own home, at a cottage, in a hotel or at a destination they choose, and he follows up by video, phone and text.
about_blocks.html: Sober Maintenance is a private addiction recovery coaching service run by one person, Trevor Smith, from Toronto. It is not a rehab centre. There are no beds, no group sessions and no clinic to walk into. Trevor meets clients in their own home, at a cottage, in a hotel or at a destination they choose, and he follows up by video, phone and text.

about_blocks.text: Trevor is a certified addiction counsellor (CCAC) and certified recovery coach (CCRC). He holds an Honours BA in cognitive science from the University of Toronto and a graduate certificate in addictions and mental health from Durham College. Before starting Sober Maintenance he spent nearly four years as a primary counsellor at a private treatment centre, and he teaches in a mental health and addictions program at a career college. He has been sober since September 2019, after about 30 years working in casinos, poker rooms and on cruise ship gaming floors.

about_blocks.text: He calls his approach the ART Method, short for Addiction Recovery Training. The idea is that staying sober is a skill you practise, so sessions mix one-to-one counselling with daily structure: journalling, mindfulness, movement or yoga, learning how the brain's reward system works, and honest review of past relapses. He uses motivational interviewing and draws on CBT, DBT and ACT.

about_blocks.text: The service suits adults who are motivated to change. That includes people who want to stop or cut back before things fall apart, people who have finished treatment and want closer support at home, and people who have relapsed several times. Gambling problems alongside alcohol or drug use are a particular focus. Trevor says plainly that he cannot work with someone who does not want to change, though families are welcome to ask for a consultation.

Anyone at risk of serious withdrawal, or in a mental health emergency, needs a hospital or a medical detox program first. Every engagement starts with a free, confidential 30-minute consultation.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Sober Maintenance

faqs.question: Is Sober Maintenance a residential rehab?

answer_blocks.text: No. Sober Maintenance is a private, one-to-one recovery coaching and addiction counselling service with no beds and no facility. Trevor Smith comes to you at home, at a cottage, in a hotel or at a destination, and also works by video. If you need live-in treatment, compare residential centres in Toronto and across Ontario.

faqs.question: How much does Sober Maintenance cost?

answer_blocks.text: A 60-minute virtual session is $175 and an in-person hour is $225, according to the Sober Maintenance website. Monthly coaching is $600 for four sessions or $1,120 for eight. The 30-day hybrid program is $5,900 CAD, longer 60 and 90-day programs start at about $15,000 and $20,000, and live-in sober companionship runs $1,200 to $2,000 a day plus travel.

answer_blocks.text: The 30-day hybrid program combines five days of in-person coaching, about eight hours a day, with ten virtual counselling sessions of 60 to 75 minutes. It also includes daily text, email or phone check-ins for the whole month, journal reflections and addiction education drawn from psychology, neuroscience and trauma-informed resources. It is available anywhere in the GTA.

faqs.question: Can a family member book on someone's behalf?

answer_blocks.text: Families can reach out for a consultation, but the person with the addiction has to want to change. Trevor states that this is not an intervention service. For concierge clients, a lawyer, physician, assistant or family member can make first contact, and an optional family track can run alongside the client's own work.

faqs.question: Is Sober Maintenance covered by insurance or OHIP?

answer_blocks.text: No insurance is listed. Sober Maintenance is private pay, and the recovery.com profile lists it as private pay only. Trevor is not a licensed psychotherapist, so check with your extended health plan before assuming any session can be claimed.

faqs.question: What happens after a program ends?

answer_blocks.text: Most clients move into monthly coaching, with a weekly session and regular check-ins by text and email. Longer programs include an integration phase where in-person days taper into virtual sessions. Concierge clients can continue on a private retainer, and the website also offers a free online workbook, Finding Meaning in Addiction Recovery.

faqs.question: How do I start with Sober Maintenance?

answer_blocks.text: Start with a free, confidential 30-minute consultation, booked online or by email at trevor@sobermaintenance.com. Next comes a virtual interview to go over your history, and then you agree on a plan together. There is no waiting list or intake desk, and Trevor handles every inquiry himself.
